errors.why: tha snyad is conventional designation (vyavahāra); 'ultimate' inverts the term.
mngon pa'i nga rgyal is abhimāna, the conceit of having attained what one has not, not pride in general.

note: Faithful list-by-list rendering of the commentary; one term inverted (conventional rendered as ultimate).

errors.english: when the substance remains, its cessation or its new arising would be stated as being the substance
errors.why: The Tibetan says that since the substance persists there is no cessation or arising, so how could these be said to be it; the 'there is none' is lost.

errors.english: That which is distinct is indeed the nature of that very thing; this is the definition of a distinct entity
errors.why: One clause: having become of a distinct nature is itself the defining mark of a difference between things; the English splits it into two claims.

note: The Sāṃkhya pariṇāma refutation is followed well overall; two sentences are garbled.

errors.english: which are the body, speech, and mind of all tathāgatas.
errors.why: The gloss 'they are all and they are tathāgatas, hence all tathāgatas; their body, speech and mind sums up the three secrets' is not translated.

fix.replace: of all tathāgatas. They are all, and they are tathāgatas, hence "all tathāgatas"; "their body, speech, and mind" sums up the three secrets. The bhagas

errors.english: referring to Locanā and so forth
errors.why: No mention of Locanā or other goddesses in the Tibetan; it says the bhaga is the form of the Blessed One Vajradhara.

note: The nidāna gloss is mostly right, but the last sentence drops the commentary's analysis and adds goddesses not in the text.
A faithful rendering of the erysipelas treatments; the plant identifications are defensible glosses.

errors.english: those that lead to a certain eighth existence
errors.why: nges par 'gyur ba means karma that necessarily leads to an eighth existence, not 'a certain' one.

errors.english: Because the parents are the masters of the body's development
errors.why: The parents are the authors of their (the eunuchs') defective body; the defectiveness, which is the point of the argument, is lost, and the two reasons are merged into a conditional.

fix.find: Because the parents are the masters of the body's development, if there is little love, there is little benefit.
fix.replace: Because the parents are the authors of their defective bodies, and because their affection is slight, the benefit received from the parents is slight.

errors.english: that would prevent them from being touched by the downfall of immediate retribution
errors.why: The Tibetan says it is by destroying that great shame and conscience that one is touched by the ānantarya fault; it does not say shame prevents it.

note: Good rendering of the Kośa discussion of ānantarya; the eunuch argument at the end is weakened.

errors.english: The cause does not produce an effect; therefore, the effect is not something to be known.
errors.why: The root verse says 'if YOUR (the realist's) cause does not produce the effect'; the English states it as Candrakīrti's own unconditional claim.

errors.english: they become objects of conceptual thought and are thus inconceivable
errors.why: bsam du med pa says that, for one who holds things to be illusion-like, this analysis has no place; it does not call the things inconceivable.

fix.find: they become objects of conceptual thought and are thus inconceivable.
fix.replace: they become objects of conceptual thought; for such a person this analysis has no place.

errors.english: Since I have said this, the same challenge and investigation applies to you as well.
errors.why: The opponent says: as for what YOU said ('does the cause produce the effect having met it or not?'), the same objection applies to you; the English puts the question in the opponent's mouth and has 'I' say it.

fix.find: some respond by saying: "Does the cause produce the effect by meeting it, or without meeting it?" Since I have said this, the same challenge and investigation applies to you as well.
fix.replace: some respond: "As for what you said ('Does the cause produce the effect by meeting it, or without meeting it?'), the same challenge and investigation applies to you as well."

note: Madhyamakāvatāra 6.170-172 with the bhāṣya; the argument's speakers and the key point of 6.171 are blurred.

errors.why: rgyud phyi ma is the Later Tantra (Uttaratantra) of the Guhyasamāja, not an 'explanatory tantra' (bshad rgyud).

errors.english: Because one should place the circle and so forth in the heart of the Wisdom Being (jñānasattva) and the Vajra Body and so forth
errors.why: What is placed is the Body-vajra and so on; the wheel and so on in the jñānasattva's heart are where it is placed. The English swaps the object and the location.

errors.english: Therefore, those three are not merely emanation and so forth.
errors.why: The others' view is given in verse, but the English turns it into prose and adds 'merely'; the verse flatly denies that they are the three, emanation and the rest.

note: Usable, but a title is mistranslated and the placement gloss and the quoted verse of the others' view are confused.

errors.english: These five together constitute individual existence (ātman) that stirs the sense of self.
errors.why: The Tibetan glosses the song word sālija as all of these taken with the conceit of self; the word being glossed is not translated.

note: A careful word-by-word gloss of the Apabhraṃśa song that tracks the Tibetan closely.
A faithful rendering of the Vairocana sādhana steps, deity iconography and seats.

errors.english: If one perceives them as profound without conceptualizing them
errors.why: med na negates both: if one has no perception of them as profound and does not conceptualize, one practises; the parallel passage on 'unfathomable' confirms this.

fix.find: If one perceives them as profound without conceptualizing them
fix.replace: If one has no perception of them as profound and does not conceptualize them

note: Otherwise accurate; one negation is lost in the first gloss, which inverts the point.
